label: Fintech Unit Economics & Valuation
description: Build a defensible unit-economics and valuation picture for a fintech: contribution margin, CAC/LTV, cohort retention, take-rate, regulatory-capital drag, and the right multiple (revenue vs gross-profit) across lending, payments and SaaS-fintech models.

claudeKnowledge.description: Comparable-company multiples and operating benchmarks for listed fintechs (Adyen, Block, PayPal, Affirm, SoFi, Nubank, Wise, dLocal), payments and lending sector reports, and prudential/own-funds frameworks (CRR/CRD, PSD2, EMD2, MiCA own-funds for CASPs). Use web search to refresh current trading multiples and any recent transaction comparables; flag retrieval date.

guidedInputs.label: Primary Fintech Model
guidedInputs.description: Which revenue archetype best describes the company? This drives the correct unit-economics formulae and the revenue-vs-gross-profit multiple choice.

guidedInputs.label: Stage & Primary Geography
guidedInputs.description: Funding stage and the main licensing/regulatory geography — sets benchmark ranges and the prudential framework to apply.

guidedInputs.label: Analysis Focus
guidedInputs.description: Which parts of the unit-economics-and-valuation chain should the analysis prioritise?

guidedInputs.label: Purpose of the Analysis
guidedInputs.description: Why is this being done? Frames the conservatism and the deliverable.

guidedInputs.label: Known Metrics, Data & Concerns
guidedInputs.description: Paste any actuals you have (revenue, TPV/volume, take-rate, CAC, gross margin, NDR, charge-offs, capital ratios) and flag known weak spots or contested assumptions.
guidedInputs.placeholder: e.g. EUR 18m net revenue, TPV EUR 2.4bn, blended take-rate 0.75%; CAC SEK 1,900, payback 14 months; gross margin 42%; own-book loan portfolio EUR 60m, annualised net charge-offs 4.8%; CET1 19% under CRR. Concern: 60% of revenue from one acquiring partner; LTV uses a 7-year life with no churn step-up.

exampleInput: We are evaluating a Series B European payments-and-embedded-finance company for a potential lead investment. They report EUR 22m net revenue (TTM), EUR 3.1bn total payment volume, and a 0.71% blended take-rate, plus a small own-book BNPL portfolio (EUR 45m) embedded at checkout. The company guides to a 6x forward net-revenue multiple at a EUR 220m pre-money. Management's deck shows LTV/CAC of 5.2x and 110% net revenue retention. Build a defensible unit-economics and valuation view: decompose the take-rate and contribution margin (net of interchange, scheme fees and processing cost), pressure-test CAC payback and the LTV assumptions (life, discount rate, churn), assess the credit-loss and regulatory-capital drag from the BNPL book, and recommend whether a revenue or gross-profit multiple is appropriate — with a comparable-company cross-check and an IC-ready recommendation on entry valuation.

exampleValues.known_data: EUR 22m net revenue TTM; TPV EUR 3.1bn; blended take-rate 0.71%; own-book BNPL portfolio EUR 45m embedded at checkout; LTV/CAC 5.2x and NRR 110% per management; guided 6x forward net-revenue multiple at EUR 220m pre-money. Concerns: LTV assumes 7-year customer life with flat churn; gross margin not disclosed (only net revenue); credit losses on the BNPL book not separately reported; revenue concentration in two acquiring partners.
